text:
Priya Rao: quick check — running into a weird edge when streaming funcalls from the Go SDK. Auth refresh happens mid-stream, and the server returns a 401 on the next chunk. SDK currently drops the stream and caller sees EOF. Thoughts on best behavior?
Marta Chen: ugh, seen that. Do we have retry metadata per-chunk? If not we can't safely rewind streaming state for funcall outputs.
Carlos Vega: can you paste minimal repro? is it an interrupted TLS conn or explicit token error on chunk request?
Priya Rao: minimal repro: start streaming, after ~30s token expires, next chunk requests return 401. code: ```go
resp, _ := client.StreamFuncCall(ctx, req)
for resp.Next() {
  chunk := resp.Recv()
  // process
}
```
No retry hook exposed for StreamFuncCall.
Jordan Li: two axes: auth vs data. For auth, we should transparently refresh and continue if the runtime supports re-auth on the same connection. For funcall structured outputs we also need to ensure partial JSON chunks aren't lost — otherwise callers get invalid schema.
Marta Chen: proposal: add a small helper in SDK: StreamWithAuthRefresh(ctx, req, refreshFn) that will automatically call refreshFn when a 401 is seen, attempt to re-auth, and resume the stream. It would only be enabled for idempotent streams or where the server supports resume tokens.
Carlos Vega: +1 but needs server contract. If server can't resume the same KV cache or function call context, resuming could be inconsistent. We should detect resume support via a header like `x-rw-resume-token`.
Priya Rao: server does return `x-rw-resume-token` on the initial stream open in our infra. I can add that to the repro. If we get that header we can request resume on re-connect with the token.
Jordan Li: then helper semantics: on 401, call refreshFn, reconnect with token, and the SDK should buffer in-memory the last incomplete JSON fragment so we can concat safely. Need a small bounded buffer to avoid OOM.
Marta Chen: alternative: stream-level checkpoints from server (JSON fence tokens) — but that's more server change. Helper can defensively handle partial chunk by keeping last N bytes until first valid JSON boundary.
Carlos Vega: also need to plumb retries/backoff for transient 5xx vs auth flow. And ensure no duplicate function invocations — funcall semantics currently at-most-once, but resume might cause re-execution if not careful. Document this.
Priya Rao: good point — my use-case is readonly tool calls (embedding lookup). So safe to retry. For mutating tools we should fail fast and surface a specific error code.
Marta Chen: action: I'll sketch the helper API this afternoon. PR should include: small in-memory tail buffer, detection of `x-rw-resume-token`, refreshFn signature, and a clear doc block about idempotency requirements.
Priya Rao: pinging for review when ready — this would unblock our integration tests. :pray:
Carlos Vega: can you add a small unit test that simulates token expiry mid-stream and server sending resume token? We can add a flaky test harness to eng-ml CI.
Jordan Li: I'll volunteer to run perf tests once PR lands — ensure buffer doesn't add CPU overhead for hot streams.
build-bot: CI: linux-go-tests failed for branch priya/stream-auth-helper — failing test: TestStreamAuthResume (timeout).
Priya Rao: ok pushed a quick fix to retry delay, new CI triggered. sorry for noise.
Marta Chen: cool. I'll start the API draft. @Carlos @Jordan any must-have shape for the refreshFn? I was thinking `func(ctx context.Context) (string, error)` returning the new token string.
Carlos Vega: that seems fine. Also allow nil to mean no refresh (fail fast). Add ctx for cancellation.
Jordan Li: optional telemetry hook would be nice: `OnResume(func(durationMs int))` to emit metrics. But can be added later.
Priya Rao: thanks all — will coordinate on the PR and tag reviewers.
Marta Chen: ETA: PR by EOD, label devex/needs-review. :rocket:
